newsitem.title: USA: US Gulf temps seen rising to above normal.
newsitem.headline: US Gulf temps seen rising to above normal.

text.p: A cold snap in the U.S Gulf region that has disrupted energy supply will ease after Monday, with temperatures reaching above normal during the next week and a half, meteorologists said.
Meanwhile, temperatures in the U.S Northeast will fluctuate between normal and slightly below normal for the next two weeks.
"The coldest temperatures are in the past for now in the (U.S.) Gulf after today," said Fred Gesser, forecaster with Weather Express Inc in Omaha, Neb.
The Houston Ship Channel is open Monday morning despite icy waters generated from winter storms that have reduced water traffic substantially, a U.S. Coast Guard port official said.
Houston Lighting and Power Co said 180,000 customers were without electric power after a winter storm passing through south Texas coated trees and power lines with a heavy coating of ice.
Temperatures in Texas have been 15 to 25 degrees below normal, but Gesser's six to 10 day forecast from January 18 through January 22 called for above normal temperatures in the U.S. Gulf region.

In the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States, temperatures are forecasted to warm to normal Tuesday through Thursday before a cold snap is expected to send temperatures eight 10 degrees below normal during the weekend, said Charlie Notis, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather in Des Moines, Iowa.
But, temperatures are seen rising from lower levels again next week.
"Temperatures are going to be normal to slightly below normal next week," said Notis.

By late next week, a cold airmass will once again move across the the Midwest into the Northeast, but the cold front will be weaker than the one experienced by the Northeast this past weekend, said meteorologist Jon Davis at Smith Barney in Chicago.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
